newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korea's LG Semicon sees '96 sales fall.
newsitem.headline: South Korea's LG Semicon sees '96 sales fall.

text.p: South Korea's LG Semicon, a unit of the L G Group, said on Friday it expected to see its 1996 sales fall to 2.2 trillion won, down from 2.5 trillion won in 1995 due to the fall in memory chip prices this year.
Facilities investment for 1997 was seen unchanged at around the 1996 level of 1.9 trillion won, the company said in a statement.
LG Semicon said it plans to expand its non-memory chip production to make up 30 percent of its product mix by the year 2005 from the current 10 percent.
"Because of the continuous fall in DRAM prices this year...sales in 1996 are seen at 2.2 trillion won, lower than last year," the company's vice president Kang Yu-sig said in the statement.
International spot prices for 16-megabit dynamic random access memory chips have fallen to around $10 per unit from $45-$50 a year ago.
LG said it hoped to become the fifth largest semiconductor manufacturer by the year 2005. It is currently ranked 13th, it said.
Shares in LG Semicon, which is a unit of LG Group, will begin trading publicly on November 9.
